meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спокойной тебе ночи и сладких снов.
examples.trans: Good night to you and sweet dreams.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Денис, скорее, мы в кино опаздываем!
examples.trans: Denis, hurry, we are running late for the cinema!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.text: Извините, но я, наверное, уже пойду.
examples.trans: Excuse me, but I will probably go now.

examples.text: Ну, наверное, в архиве где-то.
examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.

examples.text: Он, наверное, уже пришёл домой.
examples.trans: He has probably already come home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катя, а ты уже совсем готова?
examples.trans: Katya, are you completely ready already?

examples.text: Ладно, тогда уже завтра всё расскажем.
examples.trans: Alright, then we will tell everything tomorrow.

examples.text: Вы издеваетесь, это уже третье заявление!
examples.trans: Are you kidding me, this is already the third letter!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: А вы не пойдёте с нами?
examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

examples.text: Ну, в принципе, можно и пойти.
examples.trans: Well, in principle, we can go.

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, вам что-то не понравилось?
examples.trans: Good evening, did you dislike something?

meanings.en: to see someone out, to see off
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'водить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will walk out, see off', paired with 'провожать'.

examples.text: Проводите его, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Please see him out.

examples.text: Я тебя провожу.
examples.trans: I'll see you off.

examples.text: Держи свои духи. Давай я тебя провожу. Пока!
examples.trans: Here is your perfume. Let me walk you out. Bye!
